source_refs.note: Sub-heading 'Bus Topology' of 1.5 as printed (PDF 10, printed 5).

blocks.text: In bus topology, all devices are connected to a single main cable. Data travels along this cable to reach each devices. It is simple and low in cost. Failure of the main cable can stop the entire network (as shown in Figure 1.8). It is suitable for small networks. Bus topology is not good for large networks.

blocks.alt: Bus topology as printed: six devices (two desktop computers, a laptop, two servers and a printer) joined in a row by one line. Short drops from the left desktop, the laptop and the right desktop reach the thick main cable below; the drop from the rack server stops short. The main cable is drawn in two pieces with a gap in the middle, and each outer end has a terminator, labelled Terminator.
blocks.caption: Figure 1.8: Bus Topology (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 1.8).
